t.7.58.1: On the very night that Śatrughna entered the leaf-hut, on that very night Sītā too gave birth to two sons.
t.7.58.2: Then at midnight the young boys, sons of the sages, brought Vālmīki the welcome news of Sītā's auspicious delivery, saying: “O greatly radiant one, perform for him a rite of protection that destroys evil spirits.”
t.7.58.3: Hearing those words of theirs, the sage was filled with joy, and for the two of them he performed a protective rite that slays evil spirits and destroys the Rākṣasas.
t.7.58.4: Taking up a handful of kuśa grass and also a cut piece of it, the twice-born Vālmīki, by means of these two, bestowed a protective charm that destroys evil spirits.
t.7.58.5: The one of the two who was born first should be wiped clean with kuśa grass consecrated by mantras, and so he shall be known by the name Kuśa.
t.7.58.6: And the other of the two who would be born, he, well composed, is to be wiped clean by the elderly women with the lava, the lower part of the grass, and so by name he shall be Lava.
t.7.58.7: Thus those two, born as twins, will be Kuśa and Lava by name, and by the two names given by me they will be endowed with renown.
t.7.58.8: They, attentive, received that protective charm from the sage's hand, and then, freed from all impurity, performed the rite of protection for the two.
t.7.58.10: At midnight Śatrughna heard the most joyful news, and going to the leaf-hut in the night, he exclaimed, "Wonderful, wonderful!"
t.7.58.9: Thus he heard of that protective rite being performed, of the declaring of lineage and names, and of the glorification of Rāma, for Sītā's two auspicious newborn sons.
t.7.58.11: Thus, for the delighted and great-souled Śatrughna, that rainy-season night of the month of Śrāvaṇa passed by with light, swift steps.
t.7.58.12: At daybreak, the mighty one, having performed the customary morning rites, took leave of the sage with joined palms and set out again, facing westward.
t.7.58.13: Having spent seven nights on the road, he reached the bank of the Yamunā and took up his stay in the hermitage of the sages of holy renown.
t.7.58.14: There the illustrious king passed the night together with the sages headed by Bhārgava, engaged in stories of many kinds.
